svg.aria-label: How to write 呢: 8 strokes · 7 pen lifts · 8 movements
svg.title: Writing 呢
svg.desc: 8 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of 呢 (chinese), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansSC-Subset.ttf. Stroke order after Hanzi Writer Data 呢.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–8 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chanind/hanzi-writer-data/68d10a4b21150cae5e1ebbd223eed289cf32d90c/data/%E5%91%A2.json>. Source note on variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eight ordered strokes for 呢. Medians 1–3 draw the left 口 in the same order the standalone character uses and in the same upper-left third of the square that 吗 puts it in. Medians 4–6 draw 尸 — a turning top stroke, a horizontal, and a long left-falling stroke that runs past the bottom of 口 — and medians 7–8 draw 匕 tucked inside it. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all eight medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, the three internal turns and seven intervening lifts; Noto sets 尸's long falling stroke slightly steeper than the Arphic-derived source graphic.
